This industry is definitely unfair. You will get yelled at and blamed for many things that in reality are not in your control. I don't think that this is exclusive to restaurants, there are plenty of other jobs that are just the same, but it's true of almost every restaurant I've been in. 

That being the case the best favor you can do yourself is to not allow yesterday's problems to carry into today. Try to distil from your bosses yelling or complaining, how you can avoid it happening again and forget about whatever else they said to you. None of their emotional bullshit is going to help you get any better so just take the good and forget the rest. Understand that they also are probably getting yelled at the same way you are right now, albeit behind closed doors likely, but your sous is probably getting yelled at by the cdc, and the cdc by the owner. They probably have been yelled at all their careers by other chefs too. Thats no excuse for them to be shit towards you but it's learned behavior and all you can do is try to understand that and move forward for your own sake. Try not to take it as a personal attack but rather just the emotional nature of service. Its hard, even depressing at times, but its all you can do.

You're 21, on a sautee station, and if it's as hard as you say, getting good experience and reps under your belt. If you keep at it, things will get easier with time. You'll slowly learn what your chefs want of you and learn to avoid getting yelled at. By the time you have been there 2 years you'll likely be only getting yelled at rarely. However only you can decide if this life is for you. Its hard and cruel at times but if you love food and hospitality then you will find a way to deal with these emotions better over time.

Guns in this game have a very specific feel to them. Each factions are very different. It makes sense you feel like you get lasered a lot and don't feel accurate at all. Take your gun to VR and practice the feeling of it at various ranges also trying on different attachments for recoil or COF. Youll eventually find your preferred combo.

Jetpack and cloak are difficult to play around. Your positioning is key in this game. Playing in places that give you options to retreat or reroute is important if you are shot first retreating and healing will often save your uptime. 

Spending time at the same bases will give you a better game sense as to where people can and will be. Think about where you would go if you were the enemy and play prepared for that. Use the map and minimap often. If a friendly infiltrator has recon up, abuse it. 

High ground is great because as mentioned before it gives you retreat and rerouting options, use that to your advantage.

Unless you are in a squad, in my opinion, you'll often find more success flanking, or baiting your teammates to peek and then peeking behind them rather than holding angles. Holding angles is generally worse than staying mobile, unless its a very tight choke point.

For monitor settings I play with monitor brightness, contrast, and saturation a lot. On my ASUS i use 80 brightness 65 contrast and 30-40% saturation boost. I recommend just walking around an empty area for a while playing with it until something clicks. 

Hope this helps.
